Ive had this game almost since it released to early access.
I recently, finally, completed the storyline with a good friend.
Not because I didnt like the game, but because life kept getting in our way and after a while it was too long time to pickup where we had left off.
I have to say this has been one of the best gaming experiences Ive ever had in a co-op game. The locations are interesting, the puzzles can be challenging, but its never so bad that we felt lost.
I can only recommend this game to anyone  and everyone. A little lonely for single player, but just a single other person can make this a journey very worthwhile.

My only regrets is that mod support is very limited, modders have to use code injection, so most mods only tweaks existing parameters to enhance production speed of buildings, add qol features etc., theres to my knowledge still no mod that truly expands the game in any meaningful way.
It also feels like they ran out of ideas about two thirds of the way through, the resource you need for endgame crafting and tech becomes a horrible grind and when the story is done, theres really not all that much reason to keep playing, only to keep building and designing your raft.

I hope and wish Raft will see better mod support in the future, that the devs fixes this eventually, now that theyve recently finished porting to consoles and added crossplay. This could be ten times better, but the game is already an easy 8. Try it, you wont regret it.

Who knew there was such a story behind being stranded at sea and just building a raft to survive?

I honestly thought this game was just going to be a general survival game where I would spend my time collecting resources and crafting everything I needed to stay alive. Little did I know I’d end up exploring abandoned cities taken over by robots, solving puzzles, and searching for items to progress the story.

The story has been such a pleasant surprise, and I really enjoy how you uncover more of the world as you explore rather than having everything explained to you straight away.

The raft building is also incredible. There are so many possibilities for how you can design and expand your raft that I honestly want to rebuild mine 1,000 times just to try different layouts. 😂

Resources don't feel overly scarce, which I really like, although there is still a bit of a grind involved. It never feels too frustrating, though, and there's usually something worth collecting or working towards.

I went into Raft expecting a simple survival game, but it turned out to be so much more than that. The exploration, story, progression and raft building all work together really well.

Definitely one of those games I wish I'd played sooner.

While the fighting, enemies, special resource gathering, and story are all exceptionally mediocre. I have to credit the game having a unique sandbox option compared to others. In sandboxes like minecraft, an infinite world makes you feel like any build of yours is ultimately futile and small. In raft, the world is what you allow it to be. A small simple boat, or a insanely large one. Its an unspoken ruleset that I've come to enjoy. And with its limited decoration set, the term "less is more" absolutely shines through. If you want to build but the infinite/oversized scaling of games deters you from doing that, Raft might just be for you.

266 hours spent through 3 1/2 playthroughs, and to acquire every achievement throughout the game. Revisiting Raft back towards the end of July (or latter half of it), made me realize how sentimental playing it was with others as the experience is much more fascinating, yet demanding in terms of surviving and collaborating to get through the story or build out your base, or well, your raft. Coming back to it for my third full playthrough of the world with one of my friends meant so much to me and the house (The Twoplex Bungalow, or Coastal Cottage Home) made me feel beyond emotional knowing I probably won't return as I 100% complete the game (Achievement & story-wise) and did everything I could. I do wish that there was more content and decor as I had to use glitches to get creative with certain rooms and I want to memorialize mine and my friend's house on Minecraft at some point in the near future as I did miss playing this game. Commencing a world, with others more specifically, starts out as quite the challenge since you're on a 2x2 Raft in the endeavor of gathering as many resources as you can (food, materials to further expand the Raft, others for decor, bedding if someone were to die, a shelter... water... upgrades towards the raft... weaponry...), and having done the final sessions on Hard difficulty, it frankly was demanding on us where the fear of one of us getting incapacitated would take out the other and we'd either have to reset the world, or change the files to revive us (while considering getting another friend who owned the game to resuscitate us). Progression-wise, or the further you get with the story, (once you procure the electric-based blueprints or the biofuel where you're not burning through wood), the more effortless the game would become where you're not in dire need of all those constituents (You HEAVILY/SEVERELY require wood early game for EVERYTHING: Planters, upgrades, raft-related items to advance...), but once you're out of Caravan Town or Tangaroa, then you're not needing to worry as much (as I'd still like for there to be some difficulty, I think it goes in reverse where it starts off as strenuous where you have to be prudent with what you have and are ensuring you're not wasting anything towards that long haul/voyage, but as soon as you have what's essential: Smelters, Nets to catch resources, ELECTRIC ITEMS (Purifier, Grill, Juicer, Cooking Pot, Recycler, Etc), those tribulations dematerialize where you're prepared for the end game ahead of it. Far beyond it as you're prepared and destined to conquer what lies ahead. I do wish there was more or that RedBeet Interactive would make a sequel that expanded on the first (More characters/customization/decor/foods/threats/Maybe you're a scout who aids in searching for the others... Olof could escape and hunt you down...), as coming back to this game, was a thrill and now that I'm done with it, I feel nostalgic with that bittersweet goodbye to the world and the game (If I don't return to it with another group of friends or a single friend). 
And they still should've made a Clam Chowder recipe so the Big Clams could've had another use besides for Bird Nests.

The relaxing ocean atmosphere mixed with survival and exploration makes Raft easy to get addicted to.

**Highly recommended for survival and co-op fans!**

There is nothing more isolating than being alone on a few planks of wood in the middle of an infinite ocean. And yet... there isn't much more peaceful, either. This is a fantastic game to play when you want something chill or zone out with, but there's also a fair amount of action to split up the vast ocean.

Though it took me a while to get into the game, once I started unveiling the world's story (and some better gear/technology) I got hooked (no pun intended) and picked up steam fast. The game is fairly janky in some ways, but all in all I find the game (jank included - I find it quite charming in many ways, apart from the few annoying issues) very enjoyable, and I look forward to finishing the game's story. Gameplay can be a tad repetitive, particularly while you're floating between points of interest, but if you're constantly working to improve your raft you will always have something to do whether it be gathering materials, fishing, cooking, gardening or simply adding on to your raft.

I'll also add that multiplayer works very well too, though I will warn that resources spread thin between a group of two or more - the game doesn't seem to compensate for more players, so while you will have less hands on deck, a single-player session will have more resources-per-person.

There sure is a lot of garbage in the ocean (and on steam)! My time would be better spent picking up trash from my local beach, or in this case, hooking up trash and I would've felt more accomplished than anything I've achieved in this game. Let's "dive" deeper:

If you're unemployed, this game has potential. If you're employed, there are better games at a faster pace. This game is very frustrating, as any damage makes you have to rebuild part of your raft. If you die, you lose 2/3 of your inventory. At least in Minecraft you can find your items. 

In the first few hours, you're basically on a wood plank fishing up materials to expand your raft and research new gear. This is very fun for the unemployed, since you are able to feel a sense of accomplishment of gathering materials in which you are unable to irl. You then start building your raft, and of course you feel strong enough with a wood stick and full health to explore an island right? Nah, you get 3 shot by a wild boar, 2 shot by birds dropping stones; there is no counterplay. Your wood stick also does very little damage, so you're best bet is running from pigs that run 3x your pace and knock you down. Frustrating to say the least.

At my current pace, I have no motivation to get to the late game because again, time is a resource is this game does not value your time. Everything is so slow, it's like you're playing minecraft but every block you destroy takes the same time as punching a stone. It's like League of Legends but the first hour is laning phase. It's like CS2 if pistol rounds were first to 10 rounds. 

There's nothing epic about this oceanic adventure, especially when the graphics are the same as a web game, the combat is limited in terms of skill, and the exploration is unrewarding to a point where you're better staying on the raft for majority of the game. This game has potential, but the pace of the game feels tolerable only if you identify as a sloth.

Tl;dr - do not get this game if you have a life outside living on a 2x2 in the ocean. There are more rewarding games, more in depth exploration games, more building games, than Raft. I firmly believe only masochists or people who can rewind time enjoy this game. I guess people without anything else in their life may finally find some worth in fishing aboard a wooden raft in a giant ocean for...wood and plastic.
